fitting.value: 2D grid search minimizing chi^2 = sum |T_ABCD^model - T_ABCD^data|^2 with probability density P proportional to exp(-chi^2 / 2T), then linear regression of phi(lambda^2)

evidence.quote: The error function used in the least-squares minimization is simply given by the squared differences between the data closure traces and those from the parameterized model
The probability density is then recovered as $\mathcal{P}_{\chi^2}(m,\phi) \propto \exp{\left( -\frac{\chi^2}{2T} \right)}$, where $T$ is the standard deviation of the closure trace residuals

findings_qualitative.value: Frequency-dependent variations in observed ALMA closure traces of M87 cannot be explained solely by the spatial structure factor (uv-scaling with frequency) and indicate differential Faraday Rotation across the source.

evidence.loc: Prior discussion on the behaviour of the closure traces
evidence.quote: We retrieve an average deviation of the model visibilities at spws $0$ and $3$ of $(1.2\pm0.7)\%$, much lower than the average deviation computed directly from the visibilities, of $(10\pm20)\%$. findings_qualitative.value: Fitting closure traces independently per spectral window exhibits multiple local minima (degeneracies in EVPA and fractional polarization), whereas combining all spectral windows in a joint MCMC fit breaks these degeneracies.

evidence.quote: even though the $\chi^2$ parametric space presents several minima when model-fitting for each spw individually, as reported in Fig. 7, due to the degeneracies of the closure traces with the EVPA and the fractional polarization, combining all the spw seems to help breaking the degeneracies

findings_qualitative.value: Analytical exploration of a double point-source shows closure trace amplitude peaks when component EVPAs are aligned and maximum phase sensitivity to polarized intensity variations when EVPAs point in the same direction.

evidence.loc: The case of the double source
evidence.quote: First, a closure trace amplitude peak (maximum or minimum) is obtained when the EVPAs of the two components are equal. Second, the closure trace phases are more sensitive to polarization intensity variations when the EVPAs of both components point in the same direction.

claims.hypothesis: Frequency variations in the observed closure traces of M87 in ALMA Band 6 are driven by differential Faraday Rotation rather than baseline re-projection (structure factor) across frequency.
claims.experiment: Compare the fractional variation between spw 0 (213.1 GHz) and spw 3 (229.1 GHz) for Stokes I model visibilities (structure factor only) versus the directly observed visibilities.
claims.result: Model visibilities deviate by (1.2 +/- 0.7)% between spw 0 and spw 3, much smaller than the (10 +/- 20)% deviation seen in the observed visibilities.
claims.finding: The observed frequency dependence of M87 closure traces is dominated by differential Faraday Rotation rather than source structure re-projection.

evidence.loc: Prior discussion on the behaviour of the closure traces
evidence.quote: We retrieve an average deviation of the model visibilities at spws $0$ and $3$ of $(1.2\pm0.7)\%$, much lower than the average deviation computed directly from the visibilities, of $(10\pm20)\%$. Therefore, the frequency dependence seen in the observed closure traces of M87 may be related to FR.

claims.hypothesis: Parametric model-fitting to complex closure traces alone can recover source polarization parameters (EVPA, fractional polarization) and differential Faraday Rotation independent of instrumental polarization calibration.
claims.experiment: Fit a 3-component point-source polarization model to simulated ALMA closure traces using both a per-spw 2D grid search with linear EVPA(lambda^2) fitting and a multi-spw MCMC sampler with circular statistics parameterization.
claims.result: Grid search recovers RM = (0.32 +/- 0.04) x 10^7 rad/m^2 and MCMC recovers RM ~ (0.2-0.4) x 10^7 rad/m^2, both compatible with the simulated input RM of (0.35 +/- 0.04) x 10^7 rad/m^2, while multi-spw MCMC breaks single-spw degeneracies.
claims.finding: Closure-trace model fitting reliably extracts differential polarization and Faraday Rotation without requiring instrumental polarization calibration.

evidence.quote: By doing so, we obtain a value of the RM of the core component, $RM = (0.32 \pm 0.04) \times 10^7$ rad/m$^{2}$, as shown in Fig. 6, which is compatible with the expected value of $(0.35 \pm 0.04) \times 10^7$ rad/m$^{2}$.

We obtain a RM posterior distribution spread around $RM \sim (0.2-0.4) \times 10^7$ rad/m$^{-2}$, which is close to, albeit a bit lower than, the expected value of $(0.35 \pm 0.04) \times 10^7$ rad/m$^{2}$ (see Fig. 6).

claims.hypothesis: Applying the MCMC closure-trace fitting method to real ALMA Band 6 observations of M87 can recover the differential Faraday Rotation of the M87 core directly from closure observables.
claims.experiment: Run the 2-component circular-statistics MCMC closure-trace fit on the 2017 April 6 ALMA Band 6 track of M87 using a subset of 13 antennas and compare with full-array calibrated image RM synthesis.
claims.result: The MCMC posterior peaks around RM ~ (0.8-1.6) x 10^5 rad/m^2, consistent with the ~1.5 x 10^5 rad/m^2 obtained from calibrated image analysis, though with a wide posterior distribution.
claims.finding: Differential Faraday Rotation in the M87 core-jet structure can be recovered directly from real ALMA closure traces, though precision is limited by the small (~2 deg) EVPA rotation across Band 6 and the use of 13 of 33 antennas.

evidence.quote: We get a RM posterior distribution peaked around $RM \sim (0.8-1.6) \times 10^5$ rad/m$^{-2}$, being consistent with the values obtained from the image analysis.

However, the width of the RM posterior distribution is very wide (i.e., the precision of the RM is poor), likely due to the small EVPA rotation (of the order of 2 deg.) of the core across the ALMA band.

why_this_data.value: ALMA is the most sensitive mm/submm array and recorded full-array visibilities among its 33 phased antennas during the April 2017 EHT campaign on M87, where differential Faraday Rotation between the core and jet knots had already been established by calibrated image analysis.

evidence.quote: This paper concerns, as a test dataset, the ALMA observations conducted on the April 2017 EHT campaign (cite: EHTIcomplete).

why_this_method.value: Closure traces are invariant to antenna-based and direction-independent instrumental polarization (D-terms) and gain errors; MCMC and grid search are used because the chi^2 landscape is highly non-linear with multiple local minima, and circular statistics reparameterization removes the n*pi EVPA ambiguity.
